help.title: How access control works
help.intro: Every request goes through three filters. Here you manage the second one (what each role can do) and the third one (context rules).
help.scopeIntro: Some permissions (the ones showing an adjust button) also define which data they apply to:
help.scopeOwnExample: Only their own: for example, just their own tickets or tasks.
help.scopeAreaExample: Their area: the data of the people in their department.
help.scopeNote: Checking one of these permissions applies the most cautious scope; you can adjust it with the adjust button next to the checkbox.
help.appliesBody: The change is for the whole role: everyone with that role sees it once their session updates (on reload or when returning to the window). Your own session does not change unless you have that role.

identity.title: Identity
identity.body: The session is valid and the account is active.

rbac.title: Permission (RBAC)
rbac.body: One of their roles (or an exception) grants the action's permission, with its scope.

abac.title: Context (ABAC)
abac.body: Policies check the record: status, amount, who created it. The first one that matches decides.

help.rolesBody: A role groups the permissions of a job. A person has a primary role and may have additional roles: they get the sum of all (highest scope wins). E.g. HR + Inventory = both.
help.exceptionsBody: For one person, an exception replaces what their roles say for a permission (raise, lower or remove), with a reason and expiry. They are managed in the user profile.

tips.leastPrivilege: Least privilege: start with "Read only" and grant only what the job needs.
tips.duplicate: For a job similar to another, use Duplicate and adjust; don't edit a base role for a particular case.
tips.sod: Segregation of duties: whoever creates an order should not approve it; policies enforce that.
tips.test: Before closing, test with "Can they…?" in Access by person.

catalog.title: Permission catalog

errors.key: The key must use the module.action format (lowercase, digits and underscore)
errors.name: Name is required

wizard.name: What is the permission called?
wizard.nameHint: Write it as an action: what the person will be able to do.
wizard.scopeHint: Choose whether it is a plain yes/no or depends on which records they can touch.
wizard.yesNoHint: They have it or not. E.g. export reports.
wizard.ownAreaAllHint: E.g. view tickets: only theirs, their department's or all.
wizard.areaAllHint: E.g. view punches: their department's or everyone's.
wizard.sensitiveHint: Gives control over security or sensitive data: flagged for a double-check and only ADMIN grants it as an exception.
wizard.keyHint: module.action in lowercase. The key the code uses; it cannot be changed.

policies.priorityHint: Lower number = evaluated first. The first matching rule decides; if none matches, it is allowed (the permission already authorized it).
policies.noConditions: No conditions: the rule always applies (to whoever it targets).

errors.condition: Fill in the value of every condition
errors.roles: Pick at least one role or choose "Everyone"

wizard.actionHint: The rule is checked when someone with the permission tries to do this.
wizard.denyHint: The action is not allowed, even if the role has the permission.
wizard.allowHint: Allowed, and the following rules are not checked (useful as an exception).
wizard.whenHint: Conditions on the record. With several, all must be met.
wizard.someRolesHint: Pick the roles it applies to.
wizard.name: Rule name (optional)
wizard.nameHint: If left empty, the suggested one is used.
wizard.activeHint: An inactive rule is kept but not checked.

policies.explainer: Rules add conditions to a permission the role already has. Example: even if a manager can approve purchase orders, they cannot approve the ones they created. They are checked top to bottom and the first one that applies decides.

story.otherwise: Any other case → can (their role permission is enough).
story.noRules: No rules: their role permission is enough.

explorer.emptyBody: You will see their roles, what they can do in each module and where each permission comes from, the screens they see, and you can test any action.
explorer.howResolved: Effective access = current exception > highest scope among their roles > no permission. Computed by the API with the same rules it applies on every request.
explorer.questionPlaceholder: What do you want to know if {{name}} can do? E.g. create users
explorer.hasRulesHint: This action has context rules: test it with a case.

source.none: None of their roles has it

simulator.subtitle: Checks in three steps the same thing the system checks: identity, role permission and context rules.

rbac.inactivePermission: The permission is deactivated in the catalog: nobody has it.

abac.noRules: The action has no context rules: allowed.

exception.grantIntro: It's an exception: it doesn't change their role or other people. Useful to cover for someone or a temporary case.
exception.revokeIntro: Even if their role has it, it won't apply to {{name}} while the exception lasts.
exception.reasonHint: It stays in the log so others understand the exception.
